# falcon-v1.141.0 — the verified seam

A narrowed release. The cascade transport seam that v1.140 shipped as code now ships **verified**; two supervisor defects that left a vehicle unable to re-arm, or able to arm on a dead rotor, are fixed and verified; and the CI that gates all of it was rebuilt around a merge queue so that it checks what it claims, once.

## What this tag actually verifies

Four requirements reach `verified` at `falcon-v1.141.0`. They are the only claims this tag carries as verified:

| requirement | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| `SWREQ-FALCON-TRANSPORT-P01` | the cascade seam has **one** supported transport binding, with framing, handshake, tick contract and a seqlocked observer return. Verified by FV-FALCON-TRANSPORT-001/002/003 |
| `SWREQ-FALCON-PREARM-P04` | an **isolated** rotor fault blocks arming, with its own reason |
| `SWREQ-FALCON-SUPV-P02` | a failsafe latch is an in-flight device: it **clears on disarm**, and re-arming is permitted (maintainer decision, #564) |
| `SWREQ-RELAY-VGATE-P06` | the Kani scope check scopes against the right base on every event, and sweeps whenever that base is unusable; verified by a **replay** harness, not by greps |

All 61 `steps:` of the verifying artifacts were executed on the candidate's tree with stdin closed: **61 pass, 0 fail, 0 vacuous**. Every `cargo test` step ran at least one test, and `cargo kani` verified 4 harnesses in `relay-preflight` and 6 in `falcon-hitl`.

**Everything else below ships as code on main and is not verified by this release.** Where that matters, it is said inline.

## What ships as code

**The published component is a supervised vehicle, not a stabiliser (#571).** The seam is now `pulseengine:falcon-cascade@0.12.0`, adding a `pilot` interface (`configure-supervisor`, `command`), and the component wraps `FlightSupervisor`: the mode machine, the pre-arm table and every failsafe. ⚠️ **Code only:** `SWREQ-FALCON-SUPERVISOR-P01` is `implemented` and scoped **v1.142**. One known limit, stated plainly: the seam carries no calibration, so the component arms only on bring-up defaults, and a green gz gate is **not** evidence that the pre-arm table works through the seam (#414 stays open).

**The deployment model is the real chip (#591).** The AADL is now the i.MX RT1176 two-partition design: estimator on the Cortex-M4, cascade on the Cortex-M7, both at 1 kHz, joined by a seam bound to shared on-chip RAM. Both ticks' WCET is modelled as the **whole period** and is **unmeasured** (#157), so the schedulability result means "schedulable if each tick fits its period", not "it does".

**The architecture layer is derived from that model (#602, #261).** Software requirements allocated to an architecture component: **28 → 106 of 279**. `FV-FALCON-ARCH-003` checks that the components and the AADL name the same elements. ~173 requirements belong to subsystems the AADL does not model yet and stay unallocated until it does.

**Smaller:** the legacy `hover` scenario, which diverged to 74.6 m in 25 s, is retired and `flightcore` is the default; an unknown scenario now exits 2 instead of falling back to it (#595). `falcon-ekf` is no longer published, because it exported the same interface as the flight estimator (#590). `BATTERY-P03`'s claim that a single dropped sample cannot trip it now has a test that can fail (#594).

## Verification integrity

- **A merge queue replaces "require up to date"** (#588). Previously every merge sent every open PR back through a full CI cycle.
- **Kani runs once, in the queue** (#600). The 47-leg matrix had been running three times per change; at 14:10Z on 2026-10-22, 222 of the 328 queued self-hosted jobs were this matrix. A PR's Kani check now logs `DEFERRED`, never "verified", and a skip without a recorded reason fails closed.
- **The Gazebo install is bounded and retried** (#603). 5 of 21 runs had stalled on a hosted apt mirror until the 45-min timeout, ejecting queued PRs.
- **HOLD-001's bars now equal HOLD-P01's figures** (#551). v1.140 disclosed that the verdict allowed 2× the requirement's bounds. #546 stays open until this tag ships the fix.
- **A setup-bazel pin is now verified against its tag**, and a `spar analyze` failure now fails the gate (#588).

## ⚠️ Disclosures

**The verification gate runs only `falcon`-tagged artifacts** (#601). 92 artifacts holding 180 steps are never executed by any gate. Of the 25 cheap steps among them, **3 were red on main while `verified`**, for between 1 and 13 days. One of those was caused by #588's own edit. All three are fixed; the other ~155 steps are unmeasured.

**One v1.141 requirement has no architecture component, by decision.** `SWREQ-RELAY-VGATE-P06` is CI tooling. The #261 decision allocates only what the flight AADL models, and tooling is not yet modelled, so the maintainer accepted it into this release without an allocation (2026-10-23).

**A requirement's text disagrees with the model.** `SWREQ-FALCON-EKF-P04` bounds the estimator "on the target Cortex-M7"; the agreed mapping and the AADL put it on the M4. It is recorded on the estimator component, not fixed in this release.

**Review status:** `FV-RELAY-REVIEW-140` (the v1.140 diff, de-scoped from that tag) and `FV-RELAY-REVIEW-141` are the maintainer-run `/code-review ultra` gates for this tag. _[Fill in with the findings and their disposition before tagging.]_

**Still open, still flight-relevant:** the attitude ring (#270). Its anti-windup fix, which tells the ESO what the allocator actually delivered (#556), ships here **as code**, and the ring was made measurable (#557, #559). Its verification, `SWREQ-FALCON-RATE-P05` / `FV-FALCON-RATE-002`, is `implemented` and scoped **v1.142**, so do not read this tag as closing the ring. Rotor-out recovery on the gz plant (#398) is also open.

## Falsification statement

**This release is wrong if** a host speaking the published `falcon-cascade@0.12.0` binding receives an observer read whose seqlock reports coherent while its body is torn; or if a vehicle with an isolated rotor fault reaches `Armed`; or if a vehicle that failsafed in flight, then landed and disarmed, cannot be re-armed. Every one of these is shown in simulation and on the host. None has been measured on 6X-RT silicon.
